headlines.text: 2026 brought us this moment: the AEW Women's World Title found a new home as Mercedes Mone vs. Willow Nightingale battled it out, appearing on All In: London, rated 9.33 ? a five-star epic ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. After repeatedly attacking Nightingale's injured hand, Mon? locked in the Statement Maker to finally slay her last dragon and become AEW Women's World Champion at Wembley.

On this day in 2023, Eddie Kingston vs. Wheeler Yuta etched their names into history in the first-ever NJPW STRONG Openweight Title match, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.63. Kingston retained the NJPW Strong Openweight Championship over Yuta with a spinning backfist and powerbomb combination, setting up a title-for-title showdown with Castagnoli the following week.
Flash back to 2025, when Adam Priest stepped through the curtain for the first time, appearing on Collision, rated 6.59.

secondaries.text: Looking back to 2024, when Zack Gibson made their return to AEW television after 4 months away, appearing on Rampage.

Looking back to 2026, when the AEW World Heavyweight Title found a new home as Will Ospreay vs. Kenny Omega battled it out, appearing on All In: London, rated 9.64 ? the kind of match that redefines a wrestler's career ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. Ospreay's hometown crowd of over 41,000 roared through a five-star war that saw both men trade signature finishers before Ospreay finally slew Omega ? his white whale of an opponent ? to become AEW World Champion in his home country, on his second attempt at the title after falling to Strickland at Forbidden Door 2024

Turning the clock back to 2026: there was a changing of the guard for the AEW International Title as Kazuchika Okada vs. Kyle Fletcher vs. Konosuke Takeshita battled it out, appearing on All In: London, rated 8.56 ? a genuine showstealer ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. In a three-way that opened with Fletcher blindsiding his own Don Callis Family ally Okada, the Rainmaker got the last laugh, pinning his stablemate instead of Takeshita to steal the AEW International Championship right out of the Family's hands.
